formula_checks.name: creditUtilization
formula_checks.why: Zero/nonpositive limit yields 0 share and a good status, which confuses an undefined ratio with zero utilization.
formula_checks.should_be: Refuse an undefined utilization and omit its status; keep exact-ratio threshold classification for known positive limits.

formula_checks.name: creditScoreBand
formula_checks.why: Uses the stated threshold labels and inclusive lower boundaries. Does not establish a lender approval probability.
formula_checks.rests_on: Written purpose and formula, on the stated valid input domain; ordinary arithmetic

formula_checks.name: debtToIncome
formula_checks.why: Nonpositive gross income gives a zero share and good classification despite an undefined or unbounded debt ratio.
formula_checks.should_be: Refuse the ratio/status without positive gross income; state the minimum-service numerator and homeowner heuristic.

formula_checks.name: debtKind
formula_checks.why: The prose refers to a label/icon registry but does not supply its complete mapping.
formula_checks.should_be: Supply the registry’s stable kind-to-label/icon contract.

formula_checks.name: buildDebtState
formula_checks.why: Known-balance subtotal can hide debts whose balances or rates are missing; a highest-rate choice cannot be complete if a missing rate is treated as 0.
formula_checks.should_be: Return completeness and excluded-debt reasons; restrict rankings to known comparable rates.

formula_checks.name: inferDebtType
formula_checks.why: Applies the documented first-match name heuristic. It is a suggestion and must not overwrite an explicit user classification.
formula_checks.rests_on: Written purpose and formula, on the stated valid input domain; ordinary arithmetic

formula_checks.name: debtsFromOnboarding
formula_checks.why: Creates one debt only for a positive entered balance, preserves payment and converts APR percent to fraction once; property-link validation belongs outside this converter.
formula_checks.rests_on: Written purpose and formula, on the stated valid input domain; ordinary arithmetic

formula_checks.name: getDebtState
formula_checks.why: Thin storage/event seam: passes the domain result unchanged or returns no stored result. Storage correctness cannot be inferred without implementation evidence.
formula_checks.rests_on: Written purpose and formula, on the stated valid input domain; ordinary arithmetic

formula_checks.name: mortgageOddsEffect
formula_checks.why: The independent retirement projection equations/inputs are not fully specified; exact before/after probabilities cannot be recovered from this wrapper.
formula_checks.should_be: Provide the simulation’s public mathematical contract, annual cash-flow convention and date-to-payoff mapping.
formula_checks.rests_on: DEC-0364; do not inspect app code/tests

formula_checks.name: amortise
formula_checks.why: A 1200-month cap can truncate an amortizing loan without distinguishing horizon exhaustion from complete payoff; zero-balance behavior also is not explicitly stated.
formula_checks.should_be: Return a distinct horizon-exhausted state with remaining balance; never call it cleared or mathematically never.

formula_checks.name: futureValue
formula_checks.why: The stated formula divides by the monthly rate without a zero-rate branch: a positive contribution at 0% gives 0/0.
formula_checks.should_be: At zero rate return monthly contribution × months; otherwise use the annuity formula.
formula_checks.rests_on: Ordinary annuity limit as rate tends to zero

formula_checks.name: balanceGrownTo
formula_checks.why: Inherits the zero-rate 0/0 from futureValue even though a zero-return pot has a fully known future balance.
formula_checks.should_be: Use the corrected annuity reader and preserve principal plus monthly contributions at zero return.

formula_checks.name: compareMortgageToTreasury
formula_checks.why: The rate gap is a stated pretax heuristic, not a complete recommendation; lifetime comparison lacks an explicit last-payment treatment, taxes, liquidity and Treasury reinvestment assumptions.
formula_checks.should_be: Label pretax assumptions; compare full cash-flow timelines with actual final payments and disclose liquidity and reinvestment risks.

rules_held.decision_in_force: NOT A DECISION OF HIS — the lead's decision of 2026-10-24 under his rulings DEC-1923 and DEC-3523 (tenets 1 and 4), made without asking him, as his order of 2026-09-30 says. One rule for a debt in a month, in two new shared functions, MK-CF-F-235 paysInMonth and MK-CF-F-236 paymentInMonth: from its first payment to its payoff, and a balance due in full once, in its month, at its balance. A $7,200 take-home, a $3,400 budget, the $2,400 mortgage, a $250 car loan whose first payment is Oct 28, a $300 loan paid off in August and a $1,000 tax bill due in full Sep 20: September's planned surplus read +$850, the car loan and the paid-off loan counted and the tax bill left out; it reads +$400 = 7,200 − 3,400 − 2,400 − 1,000, what the Bill calendar's September holds. October's card is unchanged, $1,150. ACTUAL no longer lists the car loan as due the 28th at $0; MONTHLY RECURRING EXPENSES reads $2,400 (it read $2,650); the tax bill is on the BIG-TICKET RADAR at $1,000; Home's due-soon reminder no longer fires for a loan not yet started. MK-CF-M-047, 048 and 049 now say they print on a later month's plan card, from the grid ($7,200 / $6,050 / $1,150), and the retired surplus line and the paycheck card's SURPLUS have their own number, MK-CF-M-078 (it printed under MK-CF-M-049). To reverse: count every debt's payment in this month again, whatever its dates. One word from him reverses it.
